ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the exterior is a triangle, with the base horizontal, and the two sides intersecting upward to form a vertex. Inside the triangle there are three circles of equal radius: two circles are arranged left and right at the bottom, both tangent to the horizontal base, and tangent to each other; one circle above is located above the space between the two bottom circles, and is tangent to both bottom circles. The lower-left circle and the upper circle are both tangent to the left slanted side, and the lower-right circle and the upper circle are both tangent to the right slanted side. The problem gives that the radii of the three circles are all 1. Reasoning: Place the base as the x-axis by the coordinate method. Since the two bottom circles are both tangent to the base and have radius 1, let the center of the lower-left circle be (-1,1), and the center of the lower-right circle be (1,1). They are 2 apart, exactly tangent. The upper circle is tangent to both bottom circles, so the distance from its center to the centers of the two bottom circles is both 2. The three centers form an equilateral triangle with side length 2, so the center of the upper circle is on x=0, with coordinates (0,1+√3). The left slanted side is the common external tangent line of the lower-left circle and the upper circle. For two circles with equal radii, their common external tangent line is parallel to the line joining the two centers. The slope of the line from the lower-left circle center (-1,1) to the upper circle center (0,1+√3) is √3, so the left slanted side can be written as y=√3x+b. The distance from this line to the lower-left circle center (-1,1) should be radius 1: |√3(-1)-1+b| / √(3+1) = 1. That is |b-1-√3|/2=1. Taking the intercept corresponding to the left external tangent line gives b=3+√3. By symmetry, the right slanted side is y=-√3x+b. The vertex of the triangle is at y=b, so the height of the triangle is b. The base is on y=0, and the intersection points of the two slanted sides with the base are x=-b/√3 and x=b/√3 respectively, so the base length is 2b/√3. The area is (1/2)(2b/√3)b = b²/√3. Substitute b=3+√3: b²/√3 = (3+√3)²/√3 = (12+6√3)/√3 = 4√3+6. Therefore the area is 6+4√3.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/tangent-line route. First read from the image that the outer figure is a triangle with horizontal base; two congruent bottom circles are tangent to the base, to each other, and to the two slanted sides respectively; the top circle is tangent to both lower circles and to both slanted sides. From the text, use that all radii are 1. Place the bottom circle centers at (-1,1) and (1,1), since they are tangent to the horizontal base and to each other. The top circle center is then at (0,1+sqrt(3)), because the three centers form an equilateral triangle of side 2. The left side of the large triangle is the common external tangent to the bottom-left and top circles; since equal-radius common external tangents are parallel to the segment joining the centers, its slope is sqrt(3). Write it as y=sqrt(3)x+b and impose distance 1 from (-1,1) to the line to get b=3+sqrt(3). By symmetry the right side is y=-sqrt(3)x+b, so the triangle height is b and the base is 2b/sqrt(3). Hence area = (1/2)(2b/sqrt(3))b = b^2/sqrt(3)=6+4sqrt(3).

图像描述：图中外部是一个三角形，底边水平，两条边向上相交成顶点。三角形内部有三个等半径圆：两个圆在底部左右排列，都与水平底边相切，并且彼此相切；上方一个圆位于两底部圆之间的上方，与两个底部圆都相切。左下圆和上圆都与左斜边相切，右下圆和上圆都与右斜边相切。题目给出三个圆半径均为 1。

推理：按坐标法放置底边为 x 轴。因为两个底部圆都与底边相切且半径为 1，可令左下圆心为 (-1,1)，右下圆心为 (1,1)。它们相距 2，正好相切。

上方圆与两个底部圆都相切，所以其圆心到两个底部圆心的距离都是 2。三个圆心构成边长为 2 的等边三角形，因此上方圆心在 x=0 上，坐标为 (0,1+√3)。

左边斜边是左下圆和上方圆的共同外切线。对于两个半径相等的圆，其共同外切线平行于两圆心连线。左下圆心 (-1,1) 到上方圆心 (0,1+√3) 的连线斜率为 √3，所以左边斜边可写为 y=√3x+b。

该直线到左下圆心 (-1,1) 的距离应为半径 1：
|√3(-1)-1+b| / √(3+1) = 1。
即 |b-1-√3|/2=1。取对应左侧外切线的截距，得到 b=3+√3。

由对称性，右边斜边为 y=-√3x+b。三角形顶点在 y=b 处，所以三角形高为 b。底边在 y=0 上，两斜边与底边交点分别为 x=-b/√3 和 x=b/√3，因此底边长为 2b/√3。

面积为
(1/2)(2b/√3)b = b²/√3。
代入 b=3+√3：
b²/√3 = (3+√3)²/√3 = (12+6√3)/√3 = 4√3+6。
所以面积为 6+4√3。

method.method_draft: Parallel-offset/inradius route. From the image, view the three circle centers as forming a small equilateral triangle: the two bottom centers are joined horizontally, and the top center is above their midpoint because each pair of circles is tangent. From the text, each circle has radius 1, so the distance between any two tangent circle centers is 2. Thus the center triangle is equilateral with side 2 and inradius r_c = (2sqrt(3))/6 = sqrt(3)/3. Each side of the outer triangle is a common tangent line to the corresponding pair of unit circles, so each outer side is parallel to the corresponding side of the center triangle and lies exactly 1 unit farther outward. Therefore the large triangle is an equilateral triangle whose inradius is r_c+1 = 1+sqrt(3)/3. For an equilateral triangle with inradius r, area is 3sqrt(3)r^2. Substituting gives area = 3sqrt(3)(1+sqrt(3)/3)^2 = 6+4sqrt(3).

Image description: The diagram shows a large triangle with a horizontal base and two slanted sides. Inside it are three equal circles arranged in a triangular packing: two circles at the bottom are tangent to each other and to the base, and a third circle sits above them, tangent to both lower circles. The left side of the triangle is tangent to the upper circle and the lower-left circle; the right side is tangent to the upper circle and the lower-right circle; the base is tangent to the two lower circles.

Reasoning: Since all three circles have radius 1 and are mutually tangent, the distance between any two circle centers is 2. Thus the three centers form an equilateral triangle of side length 2. The inradius of an equilateral triangle with side 2 is (2√3)/6 = √3/3. Each side of the outer triangle is tangent to the two corresponding unit circles, so it is parallel to the corresponding side of the center triangle and lies 1 unit farther outward. Therefore the outer triangle is also equilateral, with inradius 1 + √3/3. For an equilateral triangle with inradius r, area = 3√3 r^2. Substituting r = 1 + √3/3 gives area = 3√3(1 + √3/3)^2 = 6 + 4√3.

Inside the triangle there are three circles of equal radius: two circles are arranged left and right at the bottom, both tangent to the horizontal base, and tangent to each other; one circle above is located above the space between the two bottom circles, and is tangent to both bottom circles. The lower-left circle and the upper circle are both tangent to the left slanted side, and the lower-right circle and the upper circle are both tangent to the right slanted side. The problem gives that the radii of the three circles are all 1.

Reasoning: Place the base as the x-axis by the coordinate method. Since the two bottom circles are both tangent to the base and have radius 1, let the center of the lower-left circle be (-1,1), and the center of the lower-right circle be (1,1). They are 2 apart, exactly tangent.

The upper circle is tangent to both bottom circles, so the distance from its center to the centers of the two bottom circles is both 2. The three centers form an equilateral triangle with side length 2, so the center of the upper circle is on x=0, with coordinates (0,1+√3).

The left slanted side is the common external tangent line of the lower-left circle and the upper circle. For two circles with equal radii, their common external tangent line is parallel to the line joining the two centers. The slope of the line from the lower-left circle center (-1,1) to the upper circle center (0,1+√3) is √3, so the left slanted side can be written as y=√3x+b.

The distance from this line to the lower-left circle center (-1,1) should be radius 1:
|√3(-1)-1+b| / √(3+1) = 1.
That is |b-1-√3|/2=1. Taking the intercept corresponding to the left external tangent line gives b=3+√3.

By symmetry, the right slanted side is y=-√3x+b. The vertex of the triangle is at y=b, so the height of the triangle is b. The base is on y=0, and the intersection points of the two slanted sides with the base are x=-b/√3 and x=b/√3 respectively, so the base length is 2b/√3.

The area is
(1/2)(2b/√3)b = b²/√3.
Substitute b=3+√3:
b²/√3 = (3+√3)²/√3 = (12+6√3)/√3 = 4√3+6.
Therefore the area is 6+4√3.
